901: Men who care only about pleasing their wives miss the greatest reward in life. People who want to get real work done stay away from this very habit.
902: If a man forgets his duties and lives only for his desire for his wife, whatever success he has will bring him great shame that everyone can see.
903: A man who always gives in and bows low to his wife will feel ashamed whenever he is among good people.
904: A man who is afraid of his wife loses the good that leads to a happy next life. Even if he is skilled at his work, it will never win him praise.
905: A man who is afraid of his wife will always be afraid even to do good things for good people.
906: Even if they live as grandly as the gods, men who fear their wife's slender, bamboo-like arms have no real honour.
907: A woman who has modesty and self-respect is worth far more than a man whose so-called manliness is spent doing whatever his wife orders.
908: Men who live only as their lovely wife wishes will not help their friends in need, and they will not do any good deeds.
909: Men who simply do whatever their wives command will have no good deeds, no well-earned money, and none of life's other joys either.
910: People whose minds are full of careful thought and who are strong inside will never fall into the foolishness of being ruled by love for a woman.
911: The sweet words of bangle-wearing women who want a man's money, not his love, will in the end bring him shame and trouble.
912: Some women of bad character first work out what they can get from a man and then speak sweetly about goodness. See them for what they are and stay away.
913: The fake hug of a woman who wants only money is like hugging a stranger's dead body in a dark room.
914: Wise people, who look for the true treasure of kindness, will not touch the cheap charms of women whose only goal is money.
915: People whose wisdom has been made strong by good sense will not go after the cheap pleasures of women who give themselves to anyone who pays.
916: People who care about their own good name will not go to the arms of women who show off their charm and sell cheap pleasures to anyone.
917: Only people without a steady, self-controlled heart will go to the arms of women who hug them while their own hearts are set on someone else.
918: For people without the sense to look closely, the hug of tricky, false women is said to be like being grabbed by a demon that leads them to harm.
919: The soft arms of jewel-wearing women who keep no limits are like a deep, hellish swamp that low and foolish men sink into.
920: Two-faced women, alcohol and gambling are the friends of people whom good luck has left behind.
921: People who always crave alcohol will never be feared by their enemies, and they will lose the good name they once had.
922: Do not drink alcohol. If anyone wants to drink, let it be only those who do not care whether good and wise people respect them.
923: Being drunk is painful to see even for the mother who gave birth to you. How much worse must it look to the wise?
924: The good lady called Shame (the feeling that stops us from doing wrong) turns her back on those who commit the great, hateful wrong of drinking.
925: Paying money just to buy a state where you no longer know yourself shows that you do not understand what you are doing.
926: People who are asleep are no different from the dead. In the same way, people who drink alcohol are always no different from people who drink poison.
927: People who drink in secret until their eyes droop will have their secret found out by the people of their town, who will always laugh at them.
928: A drinker should stop saying, 'I have never been drunk.' When they drink, whatever they hid in their heart comes out even more.
929: Trying to reason with a drunk person is like taking a burning torch under deep water to look for someone who has sunk.
930: When a drinker is sober and sees someone else who is drunk, does he not think that he looks just as bad when he drinks?
931: Do not want to gamble, even if you can win. Winning at gambling is like a fish swallowing the bait along with the iron hook hidden inside it.
932: Gamblers win one and lose a hundred. Can such people ever find a way to live a good life?
933: If a person keeps betting on the rolling dice without stopping, their money and the income behind it will leave them and go to others.
934: Nothing makes a person as poor as gambling. It brings many troubles and destroys a person's good name.
935: People who were proud of the dice, the gambling hall and their own skill, and would not give them up, have ended up with nothing.
936: People covered over by the bad-luck goddess called gambling will never even fill their stomachs, and they will suffer many troubles.
937: If a person spends their time in the gambling hall, it destroys both the riches they were born into and their good character.
938: Gambling wastes your money, pushes you to lie, kills your kindness, and makes you suffer.
939: If a person takes up gambling, these five things will never come to them: clothes, riches, food, fame and learning.
940: The more a gambler loses, the more they love gambling. In the same way, the more a soul suffers, the more it loves living in the body.
941: The three forces in the body that medical books name, starting with wind, cause sickness when there is too much or too little of them.
942: The body needs no medicine if a person eats only after making sure the last meal has been fully digested.
943: After your last meal is digested, eat the right amount. That is how a person who has a body can keep it going for a long time.
944: Make sure your last meal is digested. Then stick to foods that suit your body, and eat them only when you are really hungry.
945: If you eat food that suits your body and stop before you eat too much, no harm will come to your life.
946: Good health stays with a person who knows to eat a little less. In the same way, sickness stays with a person who eats far too much.
947: A person who carelessly eats far more than their stomach's fire (the body's power to digest) can handle will get sicknesses without end.
948: Find out what the sickness is, find its cause, find the way to ease it, and then treat it in the right way.
949: A trained doctor should think about the patient, how serious the sickness is, and the time or season before treating it.
950: Medicine has four parts: the patient, the doctor who cures, the medicine, and the helper who stays close to give it.
951: Doing what is right and feeling ashamed of wrong, found together as a natural habit, are seen only in people born into a good family.
952: People born into a good family never slip from these three things: good behaviour, telling the truth, and a sense of shame about doing wrong.
953: A smiling face, giving to others, kind words, and never looking down on anyone: the wise say these four are the marks of a truly good family.
954: Even if they could get crores upon crores (huge piles of money), people from good families will not do anything that brings their family down.
955: Even when they have less and less to give away, people from old, good families never lose their giving nature.
956: People who decide to live true to their spotless family name will never use tricks or do anything shameful.
957: A fault in someone from a good family stands out for everyone to see, like the dark spot on the moon high in the sky.
958: If someone who seems good shows a lack of love and kindness, people will start to doubt which family they really come from.
959: A sprout shows what kind of soil it grew in. In the same way, a person's words show what kind of family they come from.
960: If you want to be good, you must have a sense of shame about doing wrong. If you want your family to be respected, be modest and polite toward everyone.
961: Even if something seems so important that you cannot live without it, give it up if doing it would lower your self-respect.
962: People who want both a good name and true greatness will not do anything shameful, even if it would make them famous.
963: When you have plenty, be modest and gentle. When you have very little, hold your head high.
964: When people fall from their honourable place, they become like hair that has fallen from the head: worth nothing.
965: Even people as great as a mountain become small if they do something low, even something as tiny as a kunri seed (a small red bean).
966: Running after people who look down on you brings you no fame here and no place in heaven. So what good is it?
967: It is better to be called a ruined person than to live by running after people who do not respect you.
968: When your honour and greatness are being destroyed, is just keeping your body alive some medicine that will save you from death forever?
969: The yak is said to die if it loses its hair. Like that yak, people of honour would rather give up their life than live without honour.
970: The world always bows to and praises the glory of honourable people who would rather die than live in shame.
971: A person's true glory is a mind full of energy and drive. A person's shame is saying, 'I will get by without it.'
972: All living beings are born the same way. They become different in worth only because of the different work they do.
973: Low people are not great even when they sit in high places. Good people are not low even when they are in low places.
974: A faithful wife stays true by guarding herself. In the same way, greatness lasts only for a person who guards and controls themselves.
975: People who have greatness will do, in the right way, things that are very hard for others to do.
976: Small-minded people never have the thought, 'Let us respect great people and follow their ways.'
977: Even honour and high position, when they come to unworthy people, only make them act in ways that cross every limit.
978: Greatness always bows and stays modest. Smallness dresses itself up and admires itself.
979: Greatness means not being full of pride. Smallness means riding high on pride and showing off.
980: Greatness hides other people's weak points. Smallness talks about nothing but their faults.
981: For people who know their duty and choose to live with perfect character, all good things are said to be simply part of their duty.
982: The true goodness of noble people is the goodness of their character. No other kind of goodness counts as real goodness at all.
983: Love, shame at doing wrong, helping everyone, kindness toward others, and truthfulness: these five are the pillars that hold up perfect character.
984: Self-discipline is built on the goodness of not killing. Perfect character is built on the goodness of not talking about other people's wrongs.
985: The strength of capable people is their modesty. It is the weapon good people use to turn their enemies into friends.
986: If you ask what the test of perfect character is, it is being willing to accept defeat even from people who are not your equals.
987: What use is perfect character if it does not do kind things even to people who have hurt you?
988: Being poor is no shame for a person who has the inner strength called perfect character.
989: People who are called the ocean of perfect character will not change, even if the great ages of the world come to an end and change.
990: If good people ever lost their goodness, even this great earth could not carry its own weight.
991: People say that being easy for anyone to approach makes it easy to gain the good way called courtesy (being polite and kind to all).
992: Love for others and being born into a good family: these two together make up the way called courtesy.
993: Having the same body parts does not make people truly alike. Being alike in good, pleasing character is the real likeness.
994: The world praises the character of people who are useful to others because they are fair and do good.
995: Making fun of someone hurts, even as a joke. So people who understand others stay polite even toward their enemies.
996: The world keeps going because good-mannered people live in it. Without them, it would sink into the earth and die away.
997: People without good human qualities are no better than trees, even if their minds are as sharp as a file (a metal tool for sharpening).
998: Even toward people who are unfriendly and do us wrong, failing to be polite is the lowest thing a person can do.
999: For people who cannot enjoy friendly, cheerful company, this huge wide world is dark even in the middle of the day.
1000: Great riches that come to a person without good manners are like good milk spoiled by a dirty pot.
1001: A person who fills their house with huge riches but never uses them is as good as dead, because those riches do nothing at all.
1002: Thinking money can do everything, a person holds it tight and gives nothing away. That foolish mistake leads to a low, worthless birth.
1003: People who only want to pile up money and do not care about a good name are just a weight on the earth.
1004: What does a person whom no one loves think they will leave behind after they die?
1005: For people who neither give their money away nor enjoy it themselves, even crores upon crores (huge piles of money) are as good as nothing.
1006: A person who does not enjoy their great riches, and does not have it in their nature to give some to people who deserve it, is like a sickness to those riches.
1007: The riches of a person who gives nothing to the poor are like a very beautiful woman who grows old all alone.
1008: The riches of a person whom no one loves are like a poison tree bearing fruit in the middle of town.
1009: Shining riches gathered by giving up love, starving yourself and ignoring what is right will be taken by others in the end.
1010: When good rich people who are known for giving become poor for a short time, it is like a rain cloud that is empty for a while after giving its rain.
1011: True shame is pulling back from a bad deed. Other kinds of shyness are just the natural modesty of lovely young women with bright foreheads.
1012: Food, clothing and the other needs of life are the same for every living being. What makes good people special is a sense of shame.
1013: Every living being lives in a body. In the same way, perfect character lives in the good quality called shame.
1014: Isn't a sense of shame the jewel of good people? Without it, isn't their proud walk just like a sickness?
1015: People who feel ashamed of other people's wrongs as much as their own are the ones the world calls the true home of shame.
1016: Great people would not want even the whole wide world if it meant losing shame, the fence that guards them.
1017: People who live by shame will give up their life to keep it, but they will never give up shame to save their life.
1018: If a person feels no shame at things that would make others ashamed, then goodness itself (what is right) will be ashamed of that person.
1019: Slipping from good behaviour burns away the good name of your family. But once you become shameless, it burns away every good thing you have.
1020: The actions of people with no shame in their hearts are like a wooden puppet moved by strings, which only fools people into thinking it is alive.
1021: There is no greater honour than a person's promise, 'I will not stop working to help my family grow.'
1022: A family grows and lasts through long, steady work that combines two things: hard effort and full knowledge.
1023: When a person decides, 'I will lift up my family,' even the gods tie up their clothes and hurry ahead to help.
1024: For people who work hard without delay to lift up their family, the work gets done by itself, even before they have planned it.
1025: The world gathers around a person who lifts up their family without doing wrong, and treats them like one of its own family.
1026: True manliness means taking charge of and caring for the family you were born into.
1027: In battle, the heavy load falls on the brave. In the same way, in a family, the load falls on those who are able to carry it.
1028: People who work for their family cannot wait for the right time. If they are lazy or worry too much about their pride, the family falls apart.
1029: Is the body of a person who protects their family from harm made only to hold suffering?
1030: A family with no good person to hold it up will fall, like a tree, when trouble cuts at its roots.
1031: The world turns to many kinds of work, but it still has to follow the plough. So even though it is hard, farming is the best of all jobs.
1032: Farmers are like the pin that holds a wheel in place for the world, because they feed all the people who do not farm and do other work instead.
1033: Only those who live by farming and eating what they grow truly live. Everyone else bows to others for food and walks behind them.
1034: Farmers whose fields are shaded by ripe grain will see many kings' umbrellas (signs of royal power) come under their own king's umbrella.
1035: People who live by the work of their own hands never beg. They give to those who beg, without hiding what they have.
1036: If farmers stop working, even people who say, 'We have given up all our desires,' cannot keep living their way of life.
1037: If ploughed soil is dried until one measure shrinks to a quarter, the crop will grow richly without even a handful of manure.
1038: Adding manure is better than ploughing. After weeding, guarding the crop is even better than watering it.
1039: If the owner does not go to his land and look after it, the land will sulk and turn away from him, like an upset wife.
1040: When the good lady called Earth sees people sitting lazily and saying, 'We are poor,' she laughs at them.
1041: If you ask what hurts more than being poor, the only answer is being poor itself. Nothing else hurts as much.
1042: The evil thing called poverty, when it comes, takes away a person's happiness in this life and in the next life too.
1043: The hungry want called poverty destroys, all at once, a family's long history and its good name.
1044: Poverty makes even people from good families so tired and weak that low, shameful words come out of their mouths.
1045: Inside the one trouble called poverty, many kinds of sorrows gather and settle.
1046: Even when poor people speak true and wise things that they fully understand, their words are ignored and come to nothing.
1047: A person in poverty that has no goodness about it is looked at like a stranger, even by the mother who gave birth to them.
1048: A poor person asks in fear, 'Will the need that almost killed me yesterday come again today?'
1049: A person might somehow sleep in the middle of a fire, but in the middle of poverty, they cannot close their eyes at all.
1050: When very poor people do not give up worldly life completely, they only become death to other people's salt and rice-water, eating up what others have.
